newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Sept 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Brisbane yesterday rushed injured stars Michael Voss, Matthew Clarke and Jason Akermanis to Sydney for intense treatment in a bid to get the trio fit for next Saturday's AFL preliminary final against North Melbourne, while Essendon are unlikely to have half-forward Mark Mercuri for Saturday's other preliminary final against the Swans. Page 25.

Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco, who was at the centre of a drug controversy at the Atlanta Olympics, has criticised the International Amateur Athletic Federation for the delay in setting a date for his arbitration panel hearing. Page 26.

Australia's International Boxing Federation world junior-welterweight champion, Kostya Tszyu knocked South African challenger Jan Bergman out in the sixth round of their title bout in Newcastle on Saturday night. Page 28.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A 40-metre field goal struck by young Bronco's five-eighth Ben Walker sealed Brisbane's 19-16 win against South Queensland in a spiteful rugby league reserve grade final at the Sydney Football Stadium yesterday. Page 26.

Australia's Jason Stoltenberg had a place in the final of the tennis International Open snatched away from him after a remarkable comeback by German Marc-Kevin Goellner, who won the match 2-6 7-5 6-4. Page 26.

Nathan Spooner's jubilation at winning recognition in the Wallaby train-on squad for Europe was tempered yesterday by the immediate setback of his withdrawal from next Friday night's major semi-final against Warringah because of a grade-one medial ligamen strain to his left knee. Page 28.
THE AGE

Mitsubishi driver Tommi Makinen was charging towards victory in a deluge-hit Rally Australia near Perth yesterday. The seventh leg of the world championship was thrown into disarray when two stages had to be cancelled, and another two shortened,
because f dangerously high water levels. Page 15.

The National Basketball League board will meet within a fortnight to look at the recommendations of league chairman Malcolm Speed after his discussions with a number of clubs about the re-sale of their licences back to the league. Page 16.
Adelaide Lightning is aiming for its third successive Women's National Basketball League championship after thrashing the Perth Breakers 87-55 in Saturday's preliminary final in Adelaide. Page 16.
HERALD SUN
Lauren Gillett has bounced into the elite ranks of Australia's champion trampolinists by winning a gold medal at the world trampolining championships in Canada last month. Page 12.

Returning from a hamstring strain, Justin Pickering provided three goals and 25 quality touches in Frankstons's 26-point weekend victory, lifting the team into next week's Victorian Football League grand final and scoring Pickering an award. Page

Bendigo cabinet-maker Haydn Bradbury attacked relentlessly in yesterday's final stage of the A$20,000 Tour of Sunraysia to score a surprise two-second victory. Bradbury featured in almost every intermediate sprint during the criterium at Coomealla to pic up 31 bonus seconds and clinch victory over Bendigo teammate Rik McCaig. Page 81.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Roosters winger Darren Junee was knocked unconscious by a cash register roll thrown by a fan during yesterday's sudden death play-off at the Sydney Football Stadium. St George used the bomb with shattering effect winning the match 36-16 and ending SydneyCity's rugby league season. Page 1.

The State Government has scrapped plans to build a white-water rapid complex at Penrith, which was earmarked for the Olympics, because of spiralling security and transport costs. Olympics Minister Michael Knight has told the International Olympic Committe the A$12 million bill for the
project cannot be justified. Page 7.

Australia's Michael Doohan moved a step closer to his third consecutive 500cc motorcycle world championship after knocking arch-rival Alex Criville off pole position in the final minutes of practice for the Grand Prix of Catalonia yesterday. Page 27. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
